title: Found While Hunting a Tiger
description: How a British officer stumbled on the Ajanta Caves in 1819.

scenes.narration: In 1819, a British officer chasing a tiger stumbled onto one of India's greatest treasures.
scenes.image_prompt: British officer in 1819 uniform with rifle in dense Indian jungle, tiger in the bushes

scenes.narration: John Smith looks across a ravine in Maharashtra and spots the top of a carved archway.
scenes.image_prompt: carved stone archway peeking through jungle on a horseshoe-shaped cliff above a river

scenes.narration: Inside are the Ajanta Caves: around thirty Buddhist cave monuments cut into the cliff.
scenes.image_prompt: row of rock-cut cave entrances along a curved cliff face, river below

scenes.narration: The oldest date back more than two thousand years.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Buddhist monks carving a cave hall into rock by lamp light

scenes.narration: The walls are covered with paintings of the Buddha's past lives, princes, dancers and animals.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Indian mural painting of a graceful prince holding a lotus, rich colours

scenes.narration: Painters used natural pigments, and some colours still glow today.
scenes.image_prompt: artist grinding natural pigments and painting a cave wall by oil lamp

scenes.narration: Smith scratched his name and the date onto a wall inside. It's still there.
scenes.image_prompt: old graffiti signature scratched on an ancient painted cave pillar, torchlight

scenes.narration: Today it's a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Have you been to Ajanta?
scenes.image_prompt: Ajanta caves cliff in the monsoon with waterfall and green valley
